bing.title: 传统海滩小屋，索思沃尔德，萨福克遗产海岸，英格兰
bing.headline: 传统海滩小屋，索思沃尔德，萨福克遗产海岸，英格兰
bing.subtitle: 海岸边的缤纷色彩
bing.description:
在英格兰东海岸，萨福克遗产海岸融合了风吹不息的石南荒原、湿地、砾石海滩和开阔的北海景观。索思沃尔德是这里最著名的城镇之一，水域与历史在此密不可分。小镇几乎被大海、布莱斯河和周围的湿地环绕，坐落在一片狭长的半岛上；数百年来的渔业、贸易和临水生活共同塑造了这里。
色彩缤纷的木制海滩小屋是索思沃尔德最具辨识度的地标之一。它们最初是作为简易的沐浴和捕鱼棚屋而建，如今已有数百座沿海岸排列，在沙滩与天空之间增添了一道道鲜亮的色彩。有些小屋仍是备受珍爱的家庭财产，代代相传。
除了这些小屋，游客还会看到一座仍在运行的灯塔、一座伸入北海的栈桥，并可轻松前往沿海步道，欣赏英格兰一些最负盛名的风景。这是一片值得漫步探索的海岸——每一个转弯处似乎都会展开另一段关于大海的故事。

apod.title: 日食与文化
apod.description:
假设你从未听过日食。
你一生中对太阳的运作规律都了如指掌。
有一天，你目睹了天空的变化，就像今日的拼接影像一样，它展现了2026年8月12日日食两个小时的景象。
太阳消失了，只留下一个明亮、空心的光环。你会认为发生了什么事？
纵观历史，人类对日食的解读可谓五花八门，并将关于连结、重生或危险的信念 融入文化之中。
「日食」（Eclipse）一词源自希腊语「ékleipsis」，意为「离去、缺席」。在古希腊，日食象征著众神的愤怒，以及太阳遗弃人类的征兆。
对迪内族（Diné）人来说，这种天象排列是重生的时刻。出于敬畏和避免阳光的伤害，迪内族人会待在室内，直到太阳和月亮重新分开。
贝南与多哥的巴塔马利巴族（Batammariba） 相信，日食和月食期间，太阳和月亮会互相争斗，因此他们鼓励族人之间保持和平。
日食是天文学与社会之间源远流长连结的例证。
apod.explanation_en: Pretend you have never heard of a solar eclipse. The Sun’s behavior has been predictable your whole life. One day, you witness the sky transform as it does in today’s spliced image spanning two hours of the August 12, 2026 solar eclipse. The Sun disappears, leaving behind a bright, empty ring. What would you think had happened? Humans have interpreted eclipses in countless ways throughout history, embedding beliefs about connection, rebirth, or danger into culture. “Eclipse” comes from the Greek word “ ékleipsis ” meaning “abandonment”. In ancient Greece, the solar eclipse marked the anger of the gods and the Sun abandoning humanity. To the Diné people, this celestial alignment is a time of renewal. Out of respect and to avoid the danger of sunlight, the Diné stay inside until the Sun and Moon separate. The Batammariba people of Benin and Togo believe that the Sun and Moon fight during an eclipse, so the community encourages peace among themselves. Eclipses are an example of the longstanding connection between astronomy and society. Gallery: Solar Eclipse of 2026 August 12

wikipedia.title: MVIC sunset scan of Pluto
wikipedia.description: Original caption : Pluto’s Majestic Mountains, Frozen Plains and Foggy Hazes: Just 15 minutes after its closest approach to Pluto on July 14, 2015, NASA’s New Horizons spacecraft looked back toward the sun and captured this near-sunset view of the rugged, icy mountains and flat ice plains extending to Pluto’s horizon. The smooth expanse of the informally named icy plain Sputnik Planum (right) is flanked to the west (left) by rugged mountains up to 11,000 feet (3,500 meters) high, including the informally named Norgay Montes in the foreground and Hillary Montes on the skyline. To the right, east of Sputnik, rougher terrain is cut by apparent glaciers. The backlighting highlights over a dozen layers of haze in Pluto’s tenuous but distended atmosphere. The image was taken from a distance of 11,000 miles (18,000 kilometers) to Pluto; the scene is 780 miles (1,250 kilometers) wide.
